summary: Kotlas Airport (KSZ/ULKK) is a regional airport serving the city of Kotlas in Arkhangelsk Oblast, located in the northern European part of Russia along the Vychegda River. The facility operates as a medium-sized airfield and provides essential air connectivity to this remote area of the Russian north, where road and rail travel can be challenging due to long distances and harsh seasonal conditions. It primarily serves regional flights within the Northwestern Federal District.
faqs:
Q: What is the IATA code for Kotlas Airport?
A: The IATA code is KSZ, and the ICAO code is ULKK.

Q: Where is Kotlas Airport located?
A: The airport is situated near the city of Kotlas in Arkhangelsk Oblast, in northwestern Russia, at coordinates 61.236°N, 46.697°E.

Q: What type of airport is Kotlas?
A: It is classified as a medium-sized regional airport serving primarily domestic and regional flights.

Q: Can I fly internationally from Kotlas Airport?
A: The airport primarily handles regional domestic flights; for international travel, travelers typically use larger hub airports.
transport_tips: The airport is located relatively close to the city of Kotlas, making it accessible by taxi or private car in roughly 15-20 minutes from the city center. Public transport options may be limited, so arranging ground transportation in advance is recommended. During winter months, allow extra travel time as northern Russian weather can cause delays.
local_tip: Pack layers regardless of season—the Kotlas region experiences extreme temperature swings, and even brief walks between the terminal and parked aircraft can be uncomfortably cold in winter.
